ARCS kitOrganism 72week-strip

Week Strip

Show week by week how many gates entered the always-run path, and tap a week to read each fix that added one as break, repair, gate, every step cited to a commit.

States

Anatomy

#PartType roleToken (CSS variable)
1Week cellA button per week: gates wired as a large count, the week's Monday, shaded by countsurface, cyan, text
2DotsUp to three dots under the count: gates wired, a break-to-gate chain, a belief reversal (violet lifted toward text to clear 3:1)cyan, gold, violet
3ChainThree numbered steps: what broke, the fix with its commit and date, the gate it wiredtext, text-secondary, gold
4ReadoutA heading naming the picked week and its counts (a live region), any reversed beliefs as a link, then its chains or a plain empty linetext
5SourceOne line under the strip: where the counts come from, and that client names are removedtext-secondary

Usage

Use it when

  • A reader should see a hardening record over time: what broke and which check it became.
  • Every count and chain has a commit a reader could check.

Do not use it when

  • Do not invent a chain; a chain is a commit, and its public words are written from that commit's message.
  • Not for a single release's checklist: it needs weeks to mean anything.

Data it reads

FieldTypeRequiredNote
weeks[][week, monday label, gates, chains[], reversals[], withheld]yesOldest first, one per ISO week, empty weeks kept; withheld counts chains not shown.
weeks[].chains[][date, sha, scope, break, repair, gate]yesBreak and repair are reviewed public words, never the raw commit subject.
maxnumberyesThe busiest week's gate count; shading scales to it.
beliefsurlyesWhere reversal ids link.
sourcestringyesPrinted under the strip.

Access

  • Each week is a native button with aria-pressed and a label that states its date and counts. The grid is one Tab stop (roving tabindex); arrow keys, Home and End move between weeks, Enter and Space pick.
  • Only the readout heading is a polite live region, so picking a week announces its date and counts, not every chain.
  • Counts are printed, so shading and dot colour are never the only signal; the dots are hidden from screen readers because the label says the same.
  • Nothing animates. Without script the host keeps every chain as a dated list.
